test_title: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-1 (Held On: 15 Nov, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
concept: To Make a Mixture from Two Mixtures
question: Sunil started a juice (lemon syrup + water) counter. Initially, he had 145 liters of juice, which had 30% water in it. He sold 22 liters of the juice. Then he added an equal amount of lemon syrup and water. Now the ratio of water to lemon syrup became 1:2. How much water was added later on?
solution:
**Given:**

Total mixture = 145 L

Water = 30%

Sold mixture = 22 L

Water : Syrup (final) = 1 : 2

**Formula Used:**

Component = Total × Percentage

Ratio = Part ÷ Total

**Calculation:**

⇒ Initial water = 145 × 30 ÷ 100 = 43.5

⇒ Initial syrup = 145 - 43.5 = 101.5

⇒ Water removed = 22 × 30 ÷ 100 = 6.6

⇒ Syrup removed = 22 - 6.6 = 15.4

⇒ Remaining water = 43.5 - 6.6 = 36.9

⇒ Remaining syrup = 101.5 - 15.4 = 86.1

⇒ Let added water = x

⇒ Added syrup = x

⇒ Final water = 36.9 + x

⇒ Final syrup = 86.1 + x

⇒ (36.9 + x) ÷ (86.1 + x) = 1 ÷ 2

⇒ 2 × (36.9 + x) = 86.1 + x

⇒ 73.8 + 2x = 86.1 + x

⇒ x = 12.3

**∴ The correct answer is 12.3 L.**
